stem: The table below shows the average number of visits each person made to public libraries in one year, by age group, in 2000 and in 2020. Under 16: 9 visits in 2000 and 6 in 2020; 16 to 24: 4 and 3; 25 to 44: 5 and 4; 45 to 64: 7 and 5; 65 and over: 11 and 12. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The table compares how often people in five age groups visited public libraries, on average, in 2000 and 2020.

Overall, library use fell in four of the five age groups over the twenty-year period, the exception being people aged 65 and over, who were also the most frequent visitors in both years. Young adults aged 16 to 24 consistently visited libraries the least.

In 2000, the over-65s made 11 visits per person, followed by children under 16 with 9. The 45-to-64 age group averaged 7 visits, while those aged 25 to 44 and 16 to 24 made only 5 and 4 visits respectively.

By 2020, the figure for children had dropped by a third to 6 visits, and the 45-to-64 group had declined from 7 to 5. The two younger adult groups also saw a slight fall of one visit each, to 3 for the 16-to-24s and 4 for the 25-to-44s. In contrast, the oldest group was the only one to record an increase, rising marginally to 12 visits, which widened the gap between them and every other age group.
